response.message:
I've drawn the full Google Cloud flow for this synthetic qualification. Synthetic sensor readings and maintenance records come in through Pub/Sub, Dataflow and Cloud Storage. They're prepared into features in BigQuery, a model is trained and tested in Vertex AI on a later time window it never saw, each version is stored in Model Registry, and batch predictions are checked for drift. The result is a work-order draft that an operator reviews, and nothing in the design controls equipment.

The first local test only runs the synthetic data through each step with a scripted model, so it shows the wiring works but tells us nothing about prediction quality. Real model checks need actual Vertex AI training and the held-out test, and no region, account access or deployment has been approved or checked yet.

How far ahead should a warning come before a likely failure, for example 7 days? That window decides how we label the history and how we test the model.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Random splits leak future data and overstate accuracy.

response.message:
The good news is that the emulation found no failures: the flow is wired end to end, and no step tried to control equipment. It's still blocked, though, because none of our Google Cloud parts (Pub/Sub, Dataflow, Cloud Storage, BigQuery, Vertex AI training and Model Registry) has a native generator yet, and the two synthetic sources outside the build still need a plan for how we connect to them. A diagram change can't fix that. It needs product engineering work, and this report on artifact 2d598d4e can be used to reproduce it. I won't trim the design down to storage just to get a green result.

While that work happens, one answer from you will shape how the generators label and test the model. How far ahead should a warning come before a likely failure, for example 7 days?
